subject.title: fix(providers/openrouter): treat OpenRouter (URL + default route) as long-TTL-eligible for Anthropic cache_control

question: Should `OPENCLAW_CACHE_RETENTION=long` implicitly request OpenRouter's higher-cost one-hour Anthropic cache TTL on verified OpenRouter routes, or remain limited to direct Anthropic and Vertex endpoints?
rationale: The code is mechanically narrow, but this changes an existing environment-driven cost/default contract for users who already selected long retention; current public documentation explicitly describes the narrower behavior.

options.title: Approve with docs and rebase
options.body: Accept verified OpenRouter routes as long-TTL eligible, update the prompt-caching reference with the cost tradeoff, and refresh the branch on current main.

options.title: Keep the existing implicit scope
options.body: Retain direct Anthropic and Vertex-only implicit eligibility and ask for an explicit per-model retention path if OpenRouter one-hour TTL should remain opt-in.

recommendation.title: Approve with docs and rebase
recommendation.body: Accept verified OpenRouter routes as long-TTL eligible, update the prompt-caching reference with the cost tradeoff, and refresh the branch on current main.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and maintained the prior OpenRouter Anthropic cache-control implementation that this PR extends.
